content: The recommended dosage of Zithromax (azithromycin for injection) for treating adult patients with community-acquired pneumonia caused by the indicated organisms is 500 mg administered as a single daily dose via intravenous (IV) route for at least two days. Following IV therapy, azithromycin should be administered orally at a single daily dose of 500 mg, given as two 250-mg tablets, to complete a 7to 10-day course of therapy. The timing of the transition from IV to oral therapy should be determined by the physician based on the patient’s clinical response. For adult patients with pelvic inflammatory disease caused by the indicated organisms, the recommended dosage of Zithromax (azithromycin for injection) is 500 mg as a single daily dose via IV route for one or two days. This should be followed by oral azithromycin at a single daily dose of 250 mg to complete a 7-day course of therapy. The decision to switch to oral therapy should be made by the physician in accordance with the patient’s clinical response. If anaerobic microorganisms are suspected to contribute to the infection, an antimicrobial agent with anaerobic activity should be administered in combination with Zithromax. No dosage adjustment is recommended for patients with renal impairment (glomerular filtration rate [GFR] ≤ 80 mL/min). The mean area under the curve (AUC0–120) was similar in patients with GFR 10–80 mL/min compared to those with normal renal function, but it increased by 35% in patients with GFR < 10 mL/min. Caution should be exercised when administering azithromycin to patients with severe renal impairment. The pharmacokinetics of azithromycin in patients with hepatic impairment have not been established. No specific dosage adjustment recommendations can be made for patients with impaired hepatic function. Additionally, no dosage adjustment is recommended based on age or gender. The infusion concentration and rate for Zithromax (azithromycin for injection) should be either 1 mg/mL over 3 hours or 2 mg/mL over 1 hour. Zithromax should not be administered as a bolus or intramuscular injection. To prepare the solution, add 8 mL of sterile water for injection to the 500-mg vial and shake until the drug is fully dissolved. Each mL of the reconstituted solution contains 100 mg of azithromycin. The reconstituted solution is stable for 24 hours when stored below 30°C (86°F). Parenteral drug products should be visually inspected for particulate matter prior to administration, and if particulate matter is observed, the solution should be discarded. The reconstituted solution should be further diluted prior to administration as instructed. When using the Vial-Mate® drug reconstitution device, refer to the Vial-Mate® instructions for proper assembly and reconstitution. A 500-mg dose of Zithromax, diluted as described, should be infused over a period of no less than 60 minutes. Zithromax should not be administered as a bolus or intramuscular injection. Other intravenous substances, additives, or medications should not be added to Zithromax or infused simultaneously through the same IV line. At a concentration of 2 mg/mL, Zithromax (azithromycin for injection) is stable for 24 hours at or below room temperature (30°C or 86°F) or for 7 days if stored under refrigeration (5°C or 41°F).
